newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-TROUBLED PEREC INSISTS SHE CAN STILL WIN GOLD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-TROUBLED PEREC INSISTS SHE CAN STILL WIN GOLD.

text.p: Double Olympic champion Marie-Jose Perec, who made a last-minute decision to come to Athens, insisted on Friday she could still take gold over 200 metres at the sixth world championships starting on Saturday.
"If I didn't believe I could win, I wouldn't be here," the Frenchwoman said. "Obviously, I'm not as strong as I was a year ago. I think I'm at 80 percent but that could be enough."
Asked if that meant she thought she could win, she smiled: "Well, yes. It'll be a tight, open race but I do think I stand a chance."
Far from the awesome form she displayed last year to win both the 200 and the 400 metres in Atlanta, Perec lost all three of the 200 metres races she entered this year.

"It's been a funny season, I can't remember having one like that before," said the 29-year-old from Guadeloupe, whose preparation has been hampered by a stress fracture on her left shin bone followed by illness.
"Medical tests showed I was exhausted," she explained. "It's probably a virus I caught without knowing. Anyway, I've been resting for the last few weeks and I'm feeling better every day."
Perec, who first said she would miss the championships before changing her mind, brushed aside suggestions that pressure from athletics officials had made her come.
"No, it was my decision," she said. "It was hard to motivate myself for the meetings but a major championship is different. I'm a girl who runs for medals, I like that."
Perec said she would concentrate on the 200 metres because she felt she had nothing more to prove in the one-lap race.
"I've won everything in the 400 metres," said Perec, who took the world title for that distance two years ago in Gothenburg. "I showed I was the best in the world and I needed a new challenge."
She nominated Jamaican Merlene Ottey, who won 200 metres gold in the last two world championships, as her main rival for victory in Athens. "Definitely, Merlene will be the one to beat," she said.
Perec conceded she should have needed a bit more time to train to be at her best but she would not let that harm her confidence.

"To be honest, I don't really know how good I am," she said. "I've done only three meetings this year. But I'll try as hard as I can. Winning has always been my goal and I've never been afraid of anybody."

Perec, often criticised in France for her decision to live in the United States, where she trains with Los Angeles-based guru John Smith, chose to stay outside Athens with Smith's other athletes rather than with the French team.
"That's the way it is and I don't care what people say about it," she said, adding she had no plans of returning to France. "I think I'll stay in the United States for the next 10 years," she said.
Living in California, she said, could help her shine in Greece.
"Los Angeles is just as hot and just as polluted as Athens," she said.
